articles.title: Ollie Watkins’ wife Ellie returns to UK with children amid Saudi Arabia security fears after £50M transfer
articles.summary: Ollie Watkins’ big-money move to Saudi Arabia was supposed to mark an exciting new chapter for his family.
articles.body: Ollie Watkins’ big-money move to Saudi Arabia was supposed to mark an exciting new chapter for his family. Just months after leaving Aston Villa for Al-Hilal, however, the England striker is facing an unexpected change at home. His wife, Ellie Watkins, has returned to the UK with their two young children amid growing security concerns in Saudi Arabia. The decision has left the family temporarily living in two countries, while Watkins continues his football career in Riyadh. Ellie has now opened up about the sudden change through a candid TikTok update.Ellie Watkins reveals why she left Saudi Arabia with childrenEllie Watkins explained that the family's plans had changed after the situation in Saudi Arabia became increasingly concerning. In her TikTok video, she did not announce a permanent departure but made it clear that she had no fixed date for returning."We've had a bit of a plot twist"She then explained the reason behind the decision, saying:"I have come back to the UK for, hopefully, a little bit. I don't actually know when."The move comes amid renewed regional tensions and security concerns following deadly attacks in Saudi Arabia. A Houthi missile strike at Riyadh's airport in October reportedly killed 13 people and wounded more than 300. Another attack at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam also claimed two lives.Ellie addressed the situation directly in her video."There's just a little bit of conflict and things going on over in Saudi and we basically decided just to stay here until it calms down."For the couple, the decision appears to be centred on giving their children a more settled environment rather than making an immediate change to Watkins' professional commitments."I felt like I needed to do that for the kids so there is some form of normality until we can get back out there and all be together."Ollie Watkins continues Al-Hilal career after £50M Aston Villa exitWhile Ellie and the children have returned to Britain, Watkins remains in Saudi Arabia to continue playing for Al-Hilal.The £50 million-plus transfer from Aston Villa was one of the notable moves of the summer. It also marked a major change for the striker, who had spent several successful seasons in English football before accepting the opportunity in the Saudi Pro League.His performances have given Al-Hilal reasons to be pleased with the signing. Watkins has reportedly registered six goals and five assists in his first 10 appearances for the club.However, the wider situation in Saudi Arabia has affected more than individual families. The 2027 AFC Asian Cup, which the country was due to host in January, has been postponed until December 2027. Several other sporting events have also faced disruption, including the Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition.For now, Watkins faces the challenge of balancing his new career with family life across two countries. Ellie has not given a date for their return, leaving their reunion dependent on how the situation develops.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: La derrota en el Derbi contra el Athletic Club en San Mamés supuso un duro revés para la Real Sociedad. No sólo por el resultado, sino también por la polémica que rodeó a un encuentro que terminó dejando un sabor especialmente amargo en el conjunto donostiarra. Toca volver a la casilla de salida y recuperar cuanto antes las buenas sensaciones. La primera oportunidad para pasar página llegará frente al Olympique de Lyon en un partido que puede servir para recuperar la confianza y demostrar que el tropiezo en Bilbao fue sólo un accidente. Pellegrino Matarazzo había conseguido dar con la tecla. La Real se plantó en el Derbi atravesando un momento de forma tremendamente dulce después de encadenar hasta seis partidos consecutivos sin conocer la derrota entre todas las competiciones. Una dinámica que había impulsado la ilusión alrededor del equipo y reforzado la confianza de una plantilla que parecía haber encontrado por fin la regularidad. Ahora, el reto pasa por recuperar esa versión cuanto antes y evitar que la derrota ante el Athletic frene su progresión. Un escenario que puede jugar a favor de los donostiarras... siempre que consigan recuperar la solidez y la confianza que habían mostrado antes del Derbi. Lo que sí parece bastante probable es que haya espectáculo de goles. Al menos, eso es lo que sugieren los últimos registros de la Real Sociedad: en nueve de sus 10 partidos más recientes se han marcado más de 2.5 tantos. articles.title: WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights After Halloween Havoc 2026
articles.summary: In a one-off return of the Wednesday night wrestling war, WWE NXT will go head-to-head with the Blood and Guts edition of AEW Dynamite and boast a stacked card featuring several top-tier talent from Raw and SmackDown.
articles.body:
In a one-off return of the Wednesday night wrestling war, WWE NXT will go head-to-head with the Blood and Guts edition of AEW Dynamite and boast a stacked card featuring several top-tier talent from Raw and SmackDown.

Following his successful defense of the NXT Championship against Tony D'Angelo at Halloween Havoc 2026, Grayson Waller will put his gold up for grabs against SmackDown star CM Punk. WWE has already confirmed that Punk's archrival Kevin Owens will be barred from the building ahead of his No Holds Barred bout with Punk on Friday's SmackDown.

John Cena is also set to make his first appearance on the brand in over three years to announce more competitors in the upcoming John Cena Classic, while Cody Rhodes will honor the winners of the 2026 Dusty Rhodes Classic.

In other action, Kelani Jordan will defend her NXT Women's Championship in an open challenge, The Vanity Project will take on Chad Gable, Dragon Lee and Rey Fenix in six-man tag team action, and Cruz Montana and Dion Lennox will settle their score in an Unsanctioned match.

Here are the complete results, grades and reaction for the post-Halloween Havoc edition of WWE NXT as it airs live on The CW.

Chad Gable, Dragon Lee and Rey Fenix vs. The Vanity Project

Last Time in Action : Ethan Page def. Chad Gable (Raw, Nov. 2); The Vision def. Dragon Lee, Je'Von Evans and Penta (Raw, Nov. 2); Rey Fenix def. Ricky Saints (SmackDown, Oct. 30); Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno def. The Vanity Project (NXT, Oct. 27); Jackson Drake def. EK Prosper (NXT, Oct. 27).

Gable, Lee and Fenix have all been intertwined as of late in the Intercontinental Championship picture, so they had an established alliance coming into this contest.

Once the pace picked up in this match, Fenix and Lee took to the skies to wipe out Vanity Project at ringside. That allowed Gable to hit a Chaos Theory on Drake in the ring, only for the rest of Vanity Project to make the save.

Vanity Project were in control coming out of the commercial break. Drake hit a Lethal Injection on Gable for a two count soon after. After a belly-to-belly suplex from Gable to Brad Baylor, Gable made the hot tag to Fenix, who ran rampant on all three male members of Vanity Project.

After the babyfaces took turns unleashing offense on Vanity Project, Gable nailed a beautiful double German suplex. Gable and Fenix locked in submissions on Drake and Ricky Smokes while Lee pinned Baylor following an Operation Dragon.

Dragon Lee, Rey Fenix and Chad Gable defeated The Vanity Project.

As random of a match as it was, this was a blast. All six stars worked really well together and had a heck of a sprint that was all action from start to finish.

Vanity Project are obviously the NXT regulars here, but they're so great in their roles that this loss will hardly hurt them. There's also no shame in them losing to three of the very best wrestlers the main roster has to offer at the moment.

The show could have easily kicked off with John Cena's appearance or the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic finals, so it was refreshing that they went with this instead. It was the type of exciting affair that NXT was once synonymous with at one point in time.

NXT Women's Championship: Kelani Jordan vs. Paige

Last Time in Action : Kelani Jordan def. Wren Sinclair (Halloween Havoc, Oct. 31); Paige def. Nikki Bella (SmackDown, Oct. 30).

This was an open challenge. Paige received a warm welcome back from the NXT faithful, complete with chants of "Who's house? Paige's house!" Jordan gained the upper hand with a splash on Paige early on, but coming out of the commercial, the women laid each other out with dueling clotheslines.

They then traded strikes before Paige connected with a flurry of clotheslines and a classic Paige Turner. Jordan's 450 Splash was unsuccessful, though Paige came close to capturing the title with a Ram-Paige.

Jordan secured a crossface in the center of the ring before planting Paige with a DDT. Paige got the knees up for the cross-legged moonsault, but because Paige hesitated while going for her second Ram-Paige, Jordan capitalized with an inside cradle for the win.

Kelani Jordan defeated Paige to retain the NXT Women's Championship.

It looked like Iyo Sky would be answering the open challenge following the backstage interaction she and Jordan had last week, so Paige coming out instead was a pleasant surprise, especially given her own history with the NXT Women's Championship.

It was cool for the commentators to acknowledge that Paige was never beaten for the NXT Women's Championship when she had to relinquish it upon getting called up to the main roster in 2014. It's wild to think she hadn't been back on the brand since then until now.

Paige hasn't been overly protected since returning to WWE earlier this year, but it was a big deal for Jordan to beat her, nonetheless. She needed to cheated to retain her title against Wren Sinclair at Halloween Havoc but was able to score a clean win over the first-ever NXT Women's champion here.

Dusty Classic Finals: Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno vs. Hank Walker and Tank Ledger

Last Time in Action: Hank Walker and Tank Ledger def. El Hijo de Dr. Wagner Jr. and Galeno del Mal (NXT, Oct. 27); Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno def. The Vanity Project (NXT, Oct. 27).

Cody Rhodes sat in on commentary. Hank and Tank dominated the early goings and did what they could to level Dar and Moreno whenever possible.

Hank and Tank went for their finisher in the opening minutes, but Dar and Moreno were wisely able to avoid it. Dar and Moreno's simultaneous submissions were countered into powerful slams by Hank and Tank prior to the commercial break.

Moreno hit a double crossbody to Hank and Tank on the outside. After Moreno was sent spiraling into the commentary table, Hank and Tank hit top rope dives on Dar but only got a two count.

There wasn't a dull moment in the final few minutes as Dar nearly forced Walker to tap out before he was saved by Ledger. A pair of Cross Rhodes along with a high-low combination from Dar and Moreno earned the duo the victory.

Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno defeated Hank Walker and Tank Ledger to win the Dusty Rhodes Classic.

Post-match, Rhodes presented Dar and Moreno with the Dusty Classic trophy and informed them that they'll challenge Vanity Project for the NXT Tag Team Championship on next week's show. That's a quick turnaround, but it's the right call considering Dar and Moreno beat Vanity Project in a non-title bout just last week.

Neither team received a televised entrance, as that time went to televising Rhodes' entrance instead. It wasn't surprising in the slightest, but that didn't exactly put over the finals of this tournament as being important.

This year's Dusty Classic was the boost the tag team division desperately needed. The question is whether it can sustain this momentum going forward, but the pieces are there for it to be fun to follow again. Vanity Project vs. Dar and Moreno next week should be as entertaining as their last encounter was.

Unsanctioned Match: Cruz Montana vs. Dion Lennox

Last Time in Action: Cruz Montana vs. Dion Lennox ended in a double count-out (NXT, Oct. 20).

UFC's Michael Chandler served as the special guest referee. Santana went right after Lennox while Lennox was walking to the ring, which effectively established that this has been a blood feud between these two.

The first half largely consisted of them brawling around ringside. Montana attempted to hit a powerbomb through a table, and although he couldn't connect, he did put Lennox through part of a platform with a suplex soon after.

Montana was gearing up for a powerbomb on the exposed floor when Chandler appeared to talk him out of, resulting in Montana being swept off his feet post-commercial break. Lennox shoving Chandler out of the way while laying a beating on Montana gave Montana an opening and led to Montana diving over the top rope onto Lennox.

Before Montana could hit a stomp on Lennox on the exposed floor, DarkState emerged to attack Santana. The 946, a faction Santana just joined on Monday's Raw, evened the odds put Montana back in control so Montana could put down Lennox with a Spin the Block and emerge victorious.

Cruz Montana defeated Dion Lennox in an Unsanctioned match

Montana's usual entrance music didn't play when he won, presumably because he won't be using it as long as he's with The 946. Speaking of whom, the whole group posed in the ring after the match. It was an awesome visual.

This could have been even better had it not been interrupted by the commercial break and had they been allowed to push the envelope a little bit more, but for a WWE Street Fight, it was what it needed to be. The important thing is that Montana went over and can now firmly focus on his main roster future.

It wasn't that monumental seeing Jaida Parker and OTM back in NXT after only just getting called up a few months ago, but Royce Keys making his NXT TV debut here was cool. The 946 feel like a legitimate threat to The Bloodline heading into WarGames. Here's hoping WWE doesn't squander what they have with them.

John Cena Extends an Invitation for the John Cena Classic

You can tell John Cena loves the energy from the WWE Performance Center crowd based on how hyped he is to be here. The crowd sang his song word for word as he made his entrance, making the moment even more special.

After saying he missed the fans, Cena introduced the latest entrant in the John Cena Classic: Zilla Fatu. Per usual, the fans in attendance treated Fatu like a total star as he embraced Cena in the center of the ring.

Cena recounted his history with the Samoans of WWE history including Rikishi, The Rock, Roman Reigns, The Usos, Solo Sikoa and even Fatu's father Umaga. Fatu was visibly emotional while Cena took the time to praise him and offer him a spot in the Cena Classic.

Fatu told Cena that he appreciated him for the opportunity and that Raw isn't ready for what he's going to bring to the table.

This was exactly what it needed to be. Cena kept his promo short and sweet while also emphasizing that Fatu is the future of WWE (provided the company can creatively get it right with him, and there's no reason to think they won't).

We still have no idea what this Cena Classic is going to consist of exactly, but so far, we know that Cody Rhodes and Fatu are going to be a part of it and that's enough to make it feel fresh. Hopefully the rest of the field is as promising.

Coming out of the commercial break, Cena was confronted backstage by Kam Hendrix, who demanded a chance to join the Cena Classic. Instead, Cena told Hendrix that he'll be facing EK Prosper next week, and that a win would go a long way in proving himself worthy of following in Fatu's footsteps into the Cena Classic.

NXT Championship: Grayson Waller vs. CM Punk

Last Time in Action: Grayson Waller def. Tony D'Angelo (Halloween Havoc, Oct. 31). CM Punk lost the men's Money in the Bank Ladder match (Money in the Bank, Oct. 10).

Waller scored the early advantage on Punk by hitting him under the jaw and keeping control with a rest hold. Punk caught him off right before the break by pulling him into the ring apron and raining punches down upon him.

As the referee was checking in on Punk at ringside, Waller cut him off and stayed on top of Punk for several more minutes.

A little later on, Punk bested Waller after engaging in dueling suplex attempts and went on to hit his signature spots, including the running knee in the corner and the top rope elbow drop. He continued to rally momentum with a superplex off the top rope.

Punk closed in on the win with his patented GTS when Kevin Owens crashed ringside and distracted Punk long enough for him to be rolled up by Waller for the three count.

Grayson Waller defeated CM Punk to retain the NXT Championship.

It's a shame this was only just announced over the weekend at Halloween Havoc because these two could have a very entertaining war of words. That was honestly more appealing than the match itself, which was rather underwhelming for the time given.

It makes sense that Owens would make his presence felt and further his feud with Punk ahead of their No Holds Barred match on SmackDown this Friday, but WWE already announced earlier in the evening that Owens was banned from the building. Having him come out anyway was a waste and too predictable.

This wasn't the "biggest main event ever" NXT billed it as, but it was definitely a significant endorsement of Waller that he was able to get a pinfall win over Punk here. It's much better than having this end in a disqualification.

Needless to say, this show was way more about WWE trying to pop a better rating against AEW on their own night. Whether they were successful remains to be seen, but there's no denying they went all out by bringing in as many big guns as they could.

The card has promise on paper and, in a vacuum, the two hours were entertaining. Punk vs. Waller wasn't the barn burner it could have been for a variety of reasons, but Punk being in an NXT ring at all was an attraction.

It was a thumbs-up episode, but more could have been done to spotlight the current crop of competitors. Grayson Waller winning along with Zilla Fatu being endorsed by John Cena were the top two highlights, but very few (if any) NXT storylines progressed. Perhaps that's being saved for next week.

There were plenty of quality matches to make the show worthwhile, and it felt more special than the typical Tuesday night NXT, but it's clear the brand will need to replenish the pot sooner rather than later in light of all the main roster call-ups.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: Deicy Jiménez publica video y asegura tener la prueba reina de sus acusaciones contra Gustavo Petro
articles.standfirst: Escándalo de contratos: Deicy Jiménez publica video con Gustavo Petro como prueba
articles.summary: Escándalo de contratos: Deicy Jiménez publica video con Gustavo Petro como prueba
articles.body: La controversia política que envuelve al expresidente Gustavo Petro sumó un nuevo y polémico capítulo este miércoles. Deicy Jiménez, la mujer que ha estado en el centro de la opinión pública tras destapar delicadas acusaciones sobre presuntos manejos en la contratación estatal, publicó un video en su cuenta oficial de Instagram en el que aparece junto al exmandatario. La publicación rápidamente encendió las alarmas en el escenario político nacional y desató una ola de reacciones en las redes sociales, sobre un tema polémico que ya había salpicado anteriormente al expresidente de Colombia. En la descripción que acompaña el material visual, Jiménez lanzó graves afirmaciones y aseguró que esta grabación actúa como el soporte definitivo de sus denuncias: “Hoy publico este video como prueba de que estoy diciendo la verdad. Los colombianos merecen saber quién es Gustavo Petro. Confío en la justicia y le pido a esa justicia y al Gobierno que no permita que ni a mi familia ni a mí nos pase nada. Si algo nos llega a suceder hago responsable a Petro”, escribió en su perfil de Instagram. En el video difundido se alcanza a apreciar el rostro y la voz del exjefe de Estado, elementos que la defensa y la propia Jiménez esperan que se sumen al expediente que analizan las autoridades competentes. Este nuevo material se da a conocer en medio del escrutinio institucional que enfrenta el caso. Semanas atrás, Deicy Jiménez compareció ante la Corte Suprema de Justicia y la Fiscalía General de la Nación, donde entregó declaraciones y anunció la disposición de elementos tecnológicos —como su teléfono celular— para que los investigadores examinen las conversaciones, fotos y videos que respaldarían sus afirmaciones. Las denuncias iniciales, destapadas a través de entrevistas en medios de comunicación y ratificadas en diligencias judiciales, han puesto bajo la lupa procesos de contratación en entidades del orden nacional. Mientras los simpatizantes del petrismo exigen mesura ante lo que consideran ataques políticos sin verdaderos sustentos jurídicos consolidados, los sectores de oposición piden que la justicia actúe con celeridad para esclarecer la veracidad tanto del video publicado como de las denuncias de presunta red de contratación irregular. Se espera que en las próximas horas las autoridades emitan pronunciamientos oficiales sobre el impacto probatorio que este video pueda tener dentro de las indagaciones preliminares que adelanta la justicia colombiana.

articles.title: John Cena Reveals Newest Invitee to Superstar's 'Classic' Event, Salutes Gunther on WWE NXT
articles.summary: John Cena appeared on Wednesday's edition of NXT and announced Zilla Fatu as the next invitee to the inaugural John Cena Classic.
articles.body:
John Cena appeared on Wednesday's edition of NXT and announced Zilla Fatu as the next invitee to the inaugural John Cena Classic.

As Cena walked backstage before hitting the ring, he saw a poster of Gunther, who defeated the 17-time WWE world champion in his final match last December. Cena gave a tip of the cap before continuing his walk.

Cena arrived to the ring to a thunderous ovation and cheers that continued even after he started speaking.

Cena told the audience he was there to speak about the John Cena Classic and reveal the next competitor. A few moments later, Fatu entered the ring.

In a touching moment, Cena told Fatu how much his family meant to him and how much they did for him during his career. He also told Fatu how much his father, the late WWE star Umaga, meant to him.

Cena then said it was his honor to give Fatu a spot in the Classic. Fatu, of course, accepted, telling how much he appreciated Cena, thanking him for the opportunity and noting how blessed he was to receive the chance.

Last Monday, Cena announced the debut of the John Cena Classic, which will feature Raw and SmackDown superstars taking on NXT wrestlers in various matches throughout the night. Fans will vote to decide the Classic winner at the end of the night.

The event will occur live from ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex at Walt Disney World in Orlando, Florida. Cody Rhodes was previously announced as the first Classic participant.

Cena is scheduled to be on WWE screens three times between now and the Classic. The next appearance will be Friday, Nov. 13 at SmackDown in Fort Lauderdale, Florida.

articles.title: Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama calls his own number on epic coast-to-coast slam dunk
articles.summary: The San Antonio Spurs host the Dallas Mavericks at Frost Back Center on Wednesday, and as one would expect, Victor Wembanyama has been the star of the show t...
articles.body:
The San Antonio Spurs host the Dallas Mavericks at Frost Back Center on Wednesday, and as one would expect, Victor Wembanyama has been the star of the show thus far. The Mavericks found themselves trailing by 17 points at the start of the second half, with the Spurs leading the game 68-51.

And well, Wemby scored a total of 29 points in the first quarter, producing a stunning coast-to-coast dunk with seconds left on the clock, per a post on X by ClutchPoints. With the score poised at 30-26, Wemby received the ball after Kyrie Irving pushed a rebound to the edge of the three-point line, which initially allowed Wembanyama to drive forward.

He initially produced a behind-the-back dribble to get past the first Dallas defender. Wemby then drove past two players, as Cooper Flagg was found wanting on defence . Flagg expected a pass inside, which allowed Wemby to drive to the paint and bank home the dunk.

The reigning Defensive Player of the Year looked up in celebration before rushing back on defence. The Mavericks have struggled to keep up with the French phenom, whose 29 points came off 7-12 shooting despite the fact that he had missed all four of his three-point attempts in the first half.

He was also dominant on the paint, grabbing a whopping 16 rebounds in the first half alone in what was a defensive masterclass. His statline also comprised two assists, three steals, and a stunning six blocks.

The only other Spurs player who scored in double-digits in the first half was Dylan Harper, who had 13 points on 5-7 shooting. Flagg, on the other hand, has had a game to forget thus far, and could only manage four points in two quarters off 1-11 shooting.

The Mavericks have instead relied on Kyrie Irving, who had 17 points and four assists. PJ Washington added another 13 points alongside four rebounds, but the night has truly belonged to the Spurs' main man.

articles.title: “I always dreamed”: Man United hero Matheus Cunha explains joy of impressing on biggest of stages
articles.summary: Matheus Cunha had a busy final ten minutes on Tuesday night.Match impactManchester United dramatically came from 0–2 down to win 3–2 against AS Roma at Old T...
articles.body:
Matheus Cunha had a busy final ten minutes on Tuesday night.

Manchester United dramatically came from 0–2 down to win 3–2 against AS Roma at Old Trafford.

The Brazilian Cunha was the architect, scoring in the 83rd minute to equalise after a defensive mix-up.

His main moment came in the 86th minute, however, when he finished a sweeping move and jumped into the crowd to celebrate.

His evening was not over, as in added time he was sent off for a second yellow offence after pressing too vigorously and taking down the Roma defender.

After his heroics, Cunha spoke to American television show CBS Sports (via The Sun ).

The attacker revealed his feelings in the interview by explaining, "good evening, oh, I'm more anxious to do this interview than play the game, honestly!"

Reflecting on his impact on the match, he claimed, "what a magic day. Of course, apart from the red card… I always dreamed of being a part of something unbelievable. Coming here and having to come back in this very hard moment of the season."

Commenting on the tough situation that the club currently finds itself in, he stated, "I think everything, when we tried to do it, being part of Manchester United is very hard because in these kinds of moments in the season, we know we always have these kinds of comparisons with the past. We need to have these kinds of games like today, and then we'll pass the hard moment. But today was a blessed day for me."

Cunha then asserted his ambition for himself and the role he envisions for himself in the team.

He replied, "being part of this, I have a responsibility. I always talk inside about that – I need to be this kind of guy – to have the responsibility in the hard moments and the good moments. I always need to show up and be there for nights like today."

Cunha will next be in action for the club on Sunday evening at 16:30 at Old Trafford versus Aston Villa before the international break.

articles.title: OTD (5/11/1938): Gallacher Scores Final Goals As Sunderland Claim Season’s First Home Win
articles.summary: While 1937 is rightly remembered for Sunderland’s first FA Cup win, in league terms the season hadn’t been a success – at least compared to the previous camp...
articles.body:
While 1937 is rightly remembered for Sunderland's first FA Cup win, in league terms the season hadn't been a success – at least compared to the previous campaign.

After claiming the title in 1936, the lads finished the 36/37 season in eighth place – 13 points behind winners Manchester City – and finished in the same position the following season, albeit just eight points shy of champions Arsenal. The FA Cup had once again been in tantalising grasp – only for Huddersfield Town to snatch the potential of the holders retaining the trophy with a semi-final defeat.

1938/39 began with a renewed determination to reclaim the title – or at least seriously compete for it – but on this day in 1938, Sunderland finally won their first home game of the season on their sixth attempt – climbing to 6th position in the top flight in the process.

Unbeknown to anyone watching on that day, it would be the highest we'd rank in the table for eight years – and it signalled the end of an era for this talented Sunderland team. The 38/39 season saw us finish 16th, only six points off a relegation spot, after a run of just 5 wins in the season's remaining 22 games saw us drift down the table, and the following season was curtailed due to the outbreak of WW2.

But on this day back in 1938, things seemed a lot brighter as the final whistle went. A Sunderland team featuring eight of the 11 who'd played at Wembley 18 months earlier had comprehensively beaten Stoke City 3-0, turning in an excellent performance that saw Patsy Gallacher net his 100th goal in league football. He'd been on 99 since scoring away at Grimsby in March – and typically went on to score his 101st just eight minutes later.

Or did he? We'll get back to that momentarily.

By the time Gallacher got his first of the game in the 40th minute. the Sunderland team – missing only Bert Johnston, Sandy McNab and Len Duns from the 1937 side – were one up.

Sunderland had started the game excellently. Bobby Gurney and Eddie Burbanks were denied by keeper Norman Wilkinson before, on five minutes, Johnny Spuhler had a goal chalked off for offside.

Raich Carter then hit the underside of the crossbar with a great strike, which Sunderland claimed had crossed the line, but to no avail.

The ball was most definitely over the line on 15, however. Carter ran onto a through ball from Hastings, showed great strength to hold off a defender and lashed the ball into the roof of the net from the edge of the box.

The lead was almost immediately doubled; Gallacher drove the ball just wide after being set up by Burbanks. Stoke were posing a threat – England winger Stanley Matthews put in a teasing centre that Mapson dealt well with.

Sunderland had a scare when Alex Hastings appeared to be knocked unconscious heading the ball away. As the Sunderland trainer tried to revive him, a semi-conscious Hastings 'retaliated ', got to his feet, and continued the game.

Carter at one end and Matthews at the other seemed to be the players most likely to create something, but it was Sunderland who added to the scoresheet five minutes before half-time.

Sphuler's cross was headed home by Gallacher, to complete his century.

It was a proud moment for the Scotsman, although whether it was actually his 100th or not is uncertain. Records say he got 100 league goals in total for the club – so his strike that came three minutes after the break seems to have actually been his 100th.

Burbanks' cross shot was parried down towards Gallacher, who chipped the ball back over the keeper into the top of the net.

Carter was denied by the goalkeeper, while Matthews hit the post and Gurney had a goal disallowed for offside. The rest of the second half played out comfortably for the home team, but reviewing the game, Argus in the Echo suggested the side eased off and should have scored more to 'put their goalscoring account into better order'.

He was also critical of the opposition star turn Matthews, who at 23 was a regular for both club and country.

One expected much more from Matthews. He finished most of his work more like an amateurish novice than an experienced international and the great player we know him to be.

Whether it was Gallacher's 100th or 101st league goal that was scored in the 48th minute, one thing is for certain – it was his last in any competition for the lads, and he was to play only two more games for the club with whom he'd spent a decade.

The 28-year-old, whose performances had come in for some press criticism, was sold for a fee of £5500 – ironically enough, to Stoke City.

There had already been a touch of irony; his final game for Sunderland, just a fortnight after the fixture against Stoke, was a match at Roker Park against Preston North End.

The Lilywhites won 2-1, and it was perhaps a sign that this league and cup-winning team was reaching the end of its journey. As well as Gallacher's departure, the season also saw the final appearances for the club of Bobby Gurney and Jimmy Connor, while manager Johnny Cochrane resigned from his post in early March.

They say all good things have to come to an end, and while this team may have been reshaped into an even more successful one under Cochrane's replacement, Bill Murray, the advent of war firmly signalled the end to that particular story.

articles.body:
What lessons have been learned from Saturday? What have the honest and frank conversations produced? We'll find out in a matter of hours as the lads are back in action against Zagreb. Hopefully, we'll see a huge change in attitude and application, as well as our intent and team cohesion, which has been sorely lacking in recent weeks. Le Bris has been given a stay of execution – will he take advantage of it? We'll soon find out.

Roefs can't be happy at present playing in front of a team that's continually leaving him exposed – he's produced some great saves in recent European games and hopefully he has a good night tonight.

Defence: Thomas Meunier, Kevin Danso, Luke O'Nien, Dayann Methalie

Trai Hume has played a lot of football recently and with an international break looming that'll continue. Meunier needs a game so should hopefully start at right back, while Methalie will start on the left. A good show from him tonight could see him line up against Chelsea. In the centre, we're likely to see Danso return – Mukiele is still out – while O'Nien could play alongside him. The other option is Alderete, but he's completely out of sorts and needs to be taken out for a while.

Midfield: Nilson Angulo, Granit Xhaka, Jules Ahoka, Chemsdine Talbi, Malick Fofana

Talbi's inclusion in the squad is a boost and he will surely come into the team – I'd like to see him play in the 10 as he looked good there against Brentford. I think this is a game Xhaka ideally would sit out, but his form and the troubles the team's having means he probably should play; hopefully alongside Ahoka, who can provide legs and energy around him. On the wings, we need to go with two proper wingers, so hopefully Fofana will produce a good display on the left, and Angulo can carry on his good work against Poznan on the right.

We don't need to risk Brobbey, so Isidor should get an hour after 30 minutes at Coventry – he's more than capable of causing teams problems, as long as the set up behind his is decent.

articles.title: Golden State Warriors Release Injury Report Ahead of Miami Heat Matchup
articles.summary: On Thursday, the Golden State Warriors continue their six-game homestand by welcoming the Miami Heat to the Chase Center.The Warriors are on a five-game winn...
articles.body:
On Thursday, the Golden State Warriors continue their six-game homestand by welcoming the Miami Heat to the Chase Center.

The Warriors are on a five-game winning streak and will look to extend it against a struggling Heat team trying to adjust to the Giannis Antetokounmpo era.

It's also a reunion between the Warriors and Klay Thompson, who signed with the Heat in the offseason.

Golden State Warriors Injury Report vs. Miami Heat

GettyJimmy Butler III #10 of the Golden State Warriors reacts to his foul during a 119-109 Warriors win in the season opening game between the Golden State Warriors and the Los Angeles Lakers at Crypto.com Arena on October 21, 2025 in Los Angeles, California.

The Golden State Warriors released their injury report against the Miami Heat on Wednesday.

Four players are on the injury report: Jimmy Butler , Moses Moody , Kristaps Porzingis and Gui Santos .

All four players are out, with Santos as the only player considered day-to-day. Santos is dealing with left knee tendinitis.

Butler and Moody are still recovering from their respective knee injuries. Both players are expected to return later this season, possibly around the same time in January.

Meanwhile, Porzingis is still designated as "Not With Team." He was dealing with symptoms of POTS, but the Warriors are considering him as not rendering his services.

According to ESPN's Shams Charania and Anthony Slater , the Warriors are not withholding Porzingis' payments. The player and the NBPA are not contesting the decision, with Porzingis reportedly considering retirement.

Al Horford and Brandon Williams , who missed the Warriors' win against the Phoenix Suns , are both available to play.

Horford was given rest since it was the second game of a back-to-back, while Williams was dealing with a left quadriceps contusion.

The Golden State Warriors are coming off another comeback win against the Phoenix Suns. They erased a 17-point deficit to win their fifth game in a row and improved to 5-3 to start the season.

The Warriors are also 3-0 in their current six-game homestand, with wins over the Los Angeles Lakers , LA Clippers and the Suns.

They will look to replicate their success against the Miami Heat, Orlando Magic and New Orleans Pelicans .

Steph Curry is playing like an MVP, while rookie forward Yaxel Lendeborg looks like a star already.

On the other hand, the Heat will play the Clippers tonight before facing Golden State on Thursday.

They started the season 0-4 before back-to-back wins against the Atlanta Hawks and Indiana Pacers . The Lakers gave them a reality check on Monday with a blowout win, courtesy of Luka Doncic .

articles.title: Pathway to Nikita Kucherov Trade Is Now Possible for Maple Leafs
articles.summary: Shockwaves were sent throughout the National Hockey League last week when it was revealed that Tampa Bay Lightning star forward Nikita Kucherov informed the...
articles.body:
Shockwaves were sent throughout the National Hockey League last week when it was revealed that Tampa Bay Lightning star forward Nikita Kucherov informed the club that he wanted to be traded and would not sign a new contract.

Kucherov has since said that he's frustrated over what he felt was a lack of communication and respect from Bolts management rather than money.

Since then, speculation has continued to build as to which team Kucherov could potentially land with if he's ultimately dealt, and the Toronto Maple Leafs have been included among those teams.

Naturally, Lightning fans (and the club's management) are hoping that they'll get Kucherov to change his mind. But according to Kucherov's agent Dan Milstein, that ship has sailed.

Pathway For Toronto Maple Leafs To Acquire Nikita Kucherov Open After Comments From Agent

According to comments made recently by Kucherov's agent Dan Milstein, his client doesn't plan on changing his mind about his recent explosive trade request.

"I can't say anything bad about (GM) Julien (BriseBois)," Milstein said . "I believe we're on very good terms, we've done business for a very long time and he's done a very good job, he's been very successful with his job for the Tampa Bay Lightning over the years. But looking back at this past summer, I wish him and I did things a little bit different. And I'll just leave it at that, guys. But things went horribly wrong, beyond repair at this point in time, and it's unfortunate, but at the conclusion of the season, it's time to move on."

This essentially confirms Kucherov has made up his mind and believes the best course of action for his hockey career is to join a new team by next fall.

Those recent comments will certainly be on the radar of Maple Leafs GM John Chayka, who has already made several meaningful changes to the organization since taking over, including acquiring a pair of Kucherov's former Lightning teammates, Nick Paul and Darren Raddysh.

Both Nick Paul And Darren Raddysh Would Love Nikita Kucherov To Join Toronto

Paul and Raddysh, both of whom spent several years in Tampa Bay alongside Kucherov, both admitted they were surprised that he said he'd be moving on, but would absolutely welcome him on the Maple Leafs.

"That would be unbelievable to get him. He's easily one of the best players in the world. And the way he goes about his business, I think it would be awesome to have him," Raddysh said.

"You know, I'd open my arms pretty wide to have him join," Raddysh continued. "But, yeah, to add him to this group would be awesome."

"It's hard to look into those things. You never know what's really going to happen," Paul added. "But, I mean, he's a great player, and that'd be great."

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama makes history by being the first player in 50 years with these numbers
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama has continued to cement his place in history with another top-tier performance.
articles.body:
In a 14-game slate on Wednesday, there were plenty of top-tier performances. Luka Doncic was once again brilliant for the Los Angeles Lakers with a 40-point night, and the same could be said about Denver Nuggets star Nikola Jokic with another triple-double to his name.

Despite those amazing performances, they all pale in comparison when compared to San Antonio Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama. The Frenchman had the night's best performance, posting a stat line of 52 points, 24 rebounds, and eight blocks to beat the Dallas Mavericks .

Victor Wembanyama puts up historic numbers against the Mavericks

Wembanyama is the first player in 50 years to put those numbers up since Bob McAdoo and Wilt Chamberlain . For almost the entire game, the Spurs were in control against the Mavericks on Wednesday.

That was why people were raving about Wembanyama in the first half, as he already had 29 points, 15 rebounds, and five blocks at halftime.

However, the Mavericks staged a comeback in the second half. They almost won the game with a Kyrie Irving game-winner, but the Spurs defended it well, which led to a victory that matched Wembanyama's performance.

It was a magical night for the French giant, and it seems that his teammates agree with that. Everyone knows he is the Spurs' superstar, so if he performs well, the atmosphere within the Spurs organization is much better.

"When he gets in the vicinity of the paint, he's just unstoppable to guard. So I mean we just gotta keep on finding ways to get him down there and then let him operate," Spurs guard Dylan Harper said about Wembanyama's impressive performance .

Wembanyama is playing at an MVP level once again, as the Spurs have won their sixth straight game. After their slow start to the season, the Spurs fans were worried, but now, it seems that the Spurs have everyone else worried.

Despite this performance, it seems Wembanyama wants even more from himself, as he was playing while feeling a bit sick . He is demanding a lot from himself, which shows that he is not satisfied.

"It's very good because I wanted to set an example... It was good; I wish I set better screens towards the end, and made more free throws, but can't be perfect, so pretty good," Wembanyama said after the game in his post-game interview .

articles.summary: With the Raiders snapping their four-game losing streak, they have moved back up the power rankings a bit heading into Week 9.
articles.body:
Sunday the Raiders snapped their four-game losing streak with a barn-burner against the Jets . While halting the losing streak is big, giving up 33 points to the Jets is not. So, how much will it matter in the power rankings? Let's see.

Raiders spot in NFL power rankings ahead of Week 9

RB Ashton Jeanty has rushed for fewer than 50 yards in more than half of his 25 NFL starts. Not great.

Chad Graff and Josh Kendall, The Athletic -- 19

It was a tough week for Jeanty. After he made disparaging comments about the Jets, ESPN commentator and former Jets head coach Rex Ryan called him "soft as Charmin." On Sunday, the No. 6 pick in the 2025 draft was essentially benched for rookie Mike Washington. Jeanty finished with two carries for 9 yards, while Washington had 25 for 83.

The aerial stylings of Kirk Cousins, Brock Bowers and the rest of the crew delivered again, ending the Raiders' four-game losing skid in a wild, back-and-forth affair against the Jets at MetLife Stadium. Like much of Las Vegas' 2026 season, I certainly didn't expect one development to emerge: Rookie Mike Washington Jr. has taken over as the bell cow in Silver and Black, while Ashton Jeanty has become Klint Kubiak's preferred third-down, pass-catching back -- and he's making a difference in that role. Jeanty caught three passes for 64 yards in the Raiders' comeback win on Sunday, adding some more dynamism to Vegas' air game.

The Raiders bolstered their secondary by acquiring Haynes from the Patriots. The move was instrumental to winning a title that season, as he recorded an interception, two pass breakups and a tackle in Super Bowl XVIII against Washington. Haynes, who was elected to the Hall of Fame in 1997, went on to play seven seasons with the Silver and Black. In 87 games (72 starts), he totaled 18 interceptions.

They snapped a four-game losing streak by beating the Jets. The offense had a nice day with Kirk Cousins playing well. Fernando Mendoza-time can wait.

I can't be the only one who saw Klint Kubiak open the door just a smidge for Mike Washington Jr. and watched as Washington kicked the thing open, right? It's a different feel when the rookie out of Arkansas is in the backfield.

It's hard for a franchise that hasn't had much success over the past few decades to have a level head over a solid start to the season. At 4-4, the Raiders can talk themselves into being playoff contenders. That makes it hard to be a seller. It would be an even harder thing to explain to longtime fans who are dying for a taste of success or a new fan base in Las Vegas that hasn't fully embraced the Raiders yet. Realistically, the Raiders probably should be closer to sellers than they are to buyers. Could they find out if a team is willing to pay a heavy premium for Maxx Crosby like the Ravens (almost) did in March? It's not like the Ravens' concerns about Crosby's knee over the long term have vanished. However, ESPN reported the Raiders have no plans to trade Crosby. It also seems very unlikely the Raiders trade Kirk Cousins, but what if a desperate team is willing to overpay for a viable quarterback who already has 19 touchdown passes? Wouldn't they have to listen? It's not like Cousins is the future and they'll want to get Fernando Mendoza some valuable reps before the end of the season even if Cousins stays aboard. It seems foolish to be buyers when they're well behind the Broncos and Chiefs in the AFC West. articles.title: LeBron James calls Pistons star Cade Cunningham one of his ‘favorite players’ alongside Luka Doncic
articles.summary: LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers got the better of Cade Cunningham and the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday night, but the Sixers star still showed plent...
articles.body:
LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers got the better of Cade Cunningham and the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday night, but the Sixers star still showed plenty of love to the Pistons' franchise player.

After the 112-106 win at Little Caesars Arena, James put Cunningham in the same category as his former Los Angeles Lakers teammate Luka Doncic .

"I love the big guard, the big guard that can do multiple things. That's why I love Luka as well. Always stated that Luka and Cade are two of my favorite players, guys that can just do multiple things on the floor, and it's great to see where Cade is today," James said, via Chris Hine . "And yes, we have a really good relationship."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Cunningham showed exactly why in the loss. The Pistons star finished with 26 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds. Duncan Robinson added 27 points on seven 3-pointers as Detroit rallied from a 17-point deficit to make it close late.

Jaylen Brown sealed it for Philadelphia, blocking Cunningham with 37 seconds left to keep the Pistons from cutting the lead to three. Brown finished with a season-high 30 points, while Joel Embiid posted 26 points and 15 rebounds . James stuffed the stat sheet with 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists, and also became the first player in NBA history to make 16,000 field goals .

The win avenged Philadelphia's only loss of the season, a home defeat to Detroit in October. The Sixers are now 8-1 and a perfect 4-0 on the road, but James is not getting ahead of himself, even as he sees signs of his past contenders in this group.

"Those teams just had consistency throughout the whole year. We didn't want to take too many steps backwards," James said. "We understood what the assignment was, and we all held each other accountable. And I think early on, I kind of see that here as well, but it's a long season. And it's too early to be talking about the Finals and things of that nature."

"We got a good team, guys vibe with one another, guys like each other," he added. "It makes the game a lot easier when you enjoy being around people."

The Sixers visit the Cleveland Cavaliers on Friday, while the Pistons host the Lakers on Sunday.

articles.summary: It didn’t come via the hot start from Luka Dončić that’s become customary to start the season.
articles.body:
SACRAMENTO — It didn't come via the hot start from Luka Dončić that's become customary to start the season.

But the Slovenian superstar continued his dominant run to open 2026-27 Wednesday night at Golden 1 Center, recording his third straight 40-point game in the Lakers' 116-103 win over the Kings.

Dončić finished with 40 points, nine rebounds and seven assists, propelling the 7-2 Lakers to another victory.

As coach JJ Redick mentioned earlier in the week, the offensive rhythm superstar guard continues to be loud.

Almost as loud as the cowbells ringing throughout the Kings home arena.

Dončić's prolific scoring wasn't as efficient as the standard he set for himself to start the season.

He shot 11 of 23 from the field and 6 of 13 on 3-pointers (12 of 13 on free throws).

But he made the most noise when he scored 11 straight points, including three straight 3s, late in the second quarter to put the Lakers up 57-48 with just over 2 ½ minutes left in the half.

The Lakers led for the remainder of the game after the team's exchanged leads a few times in the first half.

With his performance against the Kings, Dončić became the first player in NBA history to record six consecutive games with 35-plus points, five-plus rebounds, five-plus assists and five-plus 3-pointers.

Austin Reaves added 21 points and four assists. Walker Kessler recorded 15 points, eight rebounds, four blocked shots and three steals, while Ziaire Williams and Collin Sexton each scored 10 points off the bench.

articles.summary: The LA Kings could be among the clubs making a serious push for Nikita Kucherov, as one notable insider believes. The post LA Kings Could Be Preparing for a...
articles.body:
The LA Kings may have already started laying the groundwork for a potential run at Nikita Kucherov.

According to Pierre LeBrun of The Athletic, Los Angeles is one of the teams that could make a serious push for the Tampa Bay Lightning superstar, particularly once the free-agent market opens next summer.

"They have ample cap room next summer, and 100 percent they have already talked about it. They would be all over it if possible."

That is a pretty telling assessment. The LA Kings aren't simply a team that could use another elite forward. They appear to be thinking about how Kucherov might fit into their plans, and they have the financial flexibility to make a compelling offer.

A trade is certainly worth discussing, especially with Kucherov having reportedly requested a move out of Tampa Bay. But given the Lightning's reluctance to move him and the significant return they would likely demand, free agency looks like the more realistic path for Los Angeles.

And the Kings may have a couple of reasons to make that opportunity count.

Kucherov Could Give Artemi Panarin the Superstar Running Mate He Needs

One potential selling point for the LA Kings is the possibility of pairing Kucherov with Artemi Panarin.

The two Russian stars have already been connected in speculation surrounding Los Angeles, and it's not difficult to understand the appeal. Panarin remains an elite offensive playmaker, while Kucherov is one of the most dangerous scoring threats in the NHL. Putting them together would give the Kings a formidable offensive combination.

More importantly, it would address a need that has followed Los Angeles for some time. The Kings have had capable forwards and a competitive roster, but adding another player who can consistently create offense at an elite level would change the ceiling of this group.

Kucherov would also have no shortage of options when it comes to finding chemistry. Panarin could help ease his transition, while the opportunity to play alongside other talented forwards would make Los Angeles an attractive destination.

Of course, there is a significant financial commitment involved. Kucherov is reportedly seeking a contract worth at least $20 million annually, which means the LA Kings would have to make sure the rest of their roster remains balanced. But with the cap room LeBrun highlighted, they are in a position to explore that possibility.

LA Kings Could Use Kucherov to Stay Competitive After Kopitar

There is also a bigger organizational reason for Los Angeles to pursue Kucherov.

The LA Kings want to remain competitive, and the transition beyond Anze Kopitar's era is going to be a defining moment for the franchise. Replacing a player who has been the face of the organization for so long is no easy task, particularly if the goal is to avoid slipping out of the playoff picture.

That is where Kucherov could make a major difference.

The Kings have young talent they can continue building around, but prospects and developing players don't always translate into immediate results. Kucherov would give them an established superstar capable of carrying an offense while the next generation of players takes on larger roles.

It would also send a clear message that Los Angeles has no intention of rebuilding or taking a step backward. Rather than waiting for its young core to mature before making another push, the LA Kings could accelerate that process by bringing in one of the NHL's most productive forwards.

The challenge, naturally, will be the price. A contract in the range Kucherov reportedly wants would put considerable pressure on the Kings' cap structure. But if the alternative is watching the roster gradually lose ground as Kopitar's career winds down, taking a major swing may be exactly what the organization needs.

A trade would require Tampa Bay's cooperation and a package that satisfies Julien BriseBois. Free agency gives Los Angeles more control over the process. And if LeBrun's comments are any indication, the Kings are already thinking about what that opportunity could look like.

articles.title: Runner chased by man in balaclava refuses to give up
articles.summary: An MS survivor finds strength in running community after frightening ordeal.
articles.body:
As the clocks go back and evenings become darker, many runners face a dilemma: stick to the routes they enjoy or change their habits because they do not feel safe.

Scarlett Ward refused to let fear make that decision for her.

After being chased while out on a run, she was determined not to give up a hobby that had become an important part of her life.

"They attack you twice if they make you give up what you want to do, especially something you're passionate about," said the runner, from Newcastle-under-Lyme, Staffordshire.

Running had already become far more than exercise for Ward.

Diagnosed with multiple sclerosis at the age of 28, she suffered a severe attack that left her unable to walk, talk or eat independently and was told she might never walk again.

"Being able to run whenever I want to now feels like a rebellion against my illness and something that I'll never take for granted," she said.

It was while out running in Porthill, shortly after moving to the area, that Ward had an experience which tested that determination.

She said she had been following a route through a park when she noticed a man sitting on a bench wearing a balaclava and a hood.

After running past him, she glanced over her shoulder and realised he was running after her.

"It was so scary because the path turned into a field and then into a bit of a forest and it was just absolutely horrifying," she said.

As she tried to process what was happening, one thought kept running through her mind.

"You are not prey. You will not be preyed upon."

Ward said she stopped, turned around and began shouting at the man, who then ran away. She later contacted police.

Despite the incident, she was determined not to let it stop her running.

Instead, Ward turned to social media in search of local running groups and found a community which helped rebuild her confidence.

Rob Moran, who runs with Ward as part of the group, said incidents like hers were concerning but not uncommon.

"Unfortunately, we have heard one or two stories of that going on," he said.

"It's really sad, isn't it? But it's part of the times that we live in, I think."

Moran said women often faced additional concerns when exercising alone.

"If you run on your own as a male, you can be susceptible to somebody having a go at you. You're not immune to that, being a man, are you really?"

"But certainly, the ladies, I understand why they can feel so vulnerable."

He said the group worked to ensure nobody was left behind, regardless of ability.

"There are faster runners and slower runners, but there'll be somebody running with somebody who's got a similar pace."

Chris Bailey said the running community had helped him build lasting friendships.

"I've made so many good friends through running. It is a fantastic community, there's no question," he said.

"They're such good people, all with the same mindset and goals."

Bailey said reports of runners feeling unsafe were disappointing.

"There have been several this year that we've heard of locally," he said.

"For a woman, you should never be feeling that way, that you can't go out and just run. It's not right."

He said groups such as theirs provided reassurance for people nervous about running alone.

"Nobody should be made to feel like they can't go out and run in safety," he said.

"We're very inclusive. Anybody that wants to come and join us is more than welcome."

For Ward, finding that support helped her regain confidence in a sport she never thought she would be able to enjoy again.

"It's not all doom and gloom, and the running community is so lovely that there's people to go running with wherever you look," she said.

articles.title: 76ers star Joel Embiid jokes about getting rid of 1 move after brutal stat
articles.summary: Joel Embiid and the Philadelphia 76ers keep piling up wins, but the big man’s 3-point shot has not come along for the ride. After another rough night from d...
articles.body:
Joel Embiid and the Philadelphia 76ers keep piling up wins, but the big man's 3-point shot has not come along for the ride. After another rough night from deep against the Detroit Pistons, the Sixers star joked that he might be done with the shot altogether.

Embiid went 0-of-3 from beyond the arc in Wednesday's 112-106 win at Little Caesars Arena. That dropped him to a brutal 3-of-26 from 3-point range on the season, according to ESPN's Kris Rhim, which works out to just 11.5%.

Asked about his struggles from deep, Embiid had a simple solution .

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Tonight might've been the last three I ever take," Embiid said.

It is hard to take that seriously coming from a player who has made the 3-pointer a real part of his game. Embiid shot a respectable 33.3% from deep last season, and the shot has long been a weapon that pulls opposing centers away from the paint. Head coach Nick Nurse has even pushed for more volume in the past , saying he wanted Embiid to take somewhere "in the six to nine range" of threes per game.

The good news for Philadelphia is that Embiid has still found other ways to make an impact. Against Detroit, he finished with 26 points and 15 rebounds on 8-of-18 shooting, and he went a perfect 10-of-10 from the free-throw line. He also did a lot of his damage on the offensive glass, scoring nine second-chance points.

That kind of production is exactly what the Sixers need from him. Embiid has played 39 or fewer games in each of the past three seasons, and he showed up to Media Day noticeably slimmer as he tries to stay on the floor for his first season alongside LeBron James.

So far, the new-look Sixers are rolling. Jaylen Brown led the way against the Pistons with a season-high 30 points, while James added 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists . The win avenged Philadelphia's only loss of the season and improved the team to 8-1, good for the top spot in the Eastern Conference.

Embiid and the Sixers will look to keep it going when they visit the Cleveland Cavaliers on Friday. Whether he lets one fly from deep in that game remains to be seen.

articles.title: Niceville's season comes to an end on Pace last-second TD
articles.summary: Niceville football put itself in position to win a District 1-5A title, but mistakes in crunch time led to heartbreak.
articles.body:
Niceville loses on last-second Pace touchdown

NICEVILLE — In today's Maxpreps-driven, Wild Wild West atmosphere of Florida high school football, where every two years a new playoff format enters the foray and coaches are jockeying for position in a non-transparent formula, there's a thin line between district champ and sitting out the playoffs.

Niceville went from the former to the latter in the final 20 seconds of Wednesday night's District 1-5A title game against Pace at Eagle Stadium.

UP 25-24 with 20 seconds left, the Eagles had done everything in their power to hoist district hardware and flip the narrative on Adron Robinson's first year at the helm. Deagan McCoy drove the Eagles 79 yards in 2:34, the junior connecting with Jakobe Gilyard for a 14-yard touchdown and then Caleb Leonard for the go-ahead 2-point conversion on a gutsy decision by Robinson. Only, a mistake was made. Leonard spiked the ball to draw the unsportsmanlike flag, turning a routine touchback on the ensuing kickoff into a Pace opportunity with the ball moved 15 yards back.

Still, only 20 seconds remained. Not an eternity.

The ensuing kick was meant to go up the left side, but instead it stayed straight down the middle with daylight for days. Pace returned the kick inside the Eagles' 20 and drew a facemask on the back end, placing the ball at Niceville's 7 with 8 seconds left. Makael Williams converted on the next play, scoring his fourth touchdown on a night he's carry the ball 24 times for 128 yards.

Cue the Patriots' celebration, Pace winning its third straight district title on a 31-25 win as it improved to 7-2 (4-0). Niceville, meanwhile, falls to 4-6 (3-1), its playoff resume lacking that marquee win they so desperately needed.

The Eagles can only blame themselves. Niceville led for much of the night, Kody Martin's defense delivering a statement out of the gates with an 86-yard pick six by DJ Stafford and holding the Patriots to 10 first-half points. Before the half, McCoy connected with Malachi White for a 28-yard touchdown and Jason Leach recovered a fumble on the ensuing Pace drive, Nate Martinez splitting the uprights on a 35-yarder to put the Eagles up 17-10 at half.

Pace's defense wouldn't allow much after, the Patriots disrupting the heavy package, forcing a McCoy interception and limiting Gilyard to just 33 rushing yards and Niceville's ground game to 81 yards overall. Meanwhile, Williams kept chipping away and scored three second-half touchdowns.

The last followed two costly Niceville mistakes, and when the margins are razor thin, there's no room for them in 5A.

"The Game" hasn't lived up to the billing it once did back in the early 1990s, and Wednesday was no different as Choctaw defeated Fort Walton for the sixth straight time in a 49-13 route.

Von Keller and Dante Whudbee both rushed for a pair of scores, Baker Giles connected with Noah Calderon for two of his three touchdowns and the Big Green finished the regular season on a seven-game win streak to improve to 7-2 and finish the District 1-4A slate unbeaten headed into Friday's bracket reveal by the FHSAA.

articles.title: Lakers player grades: Another 40-point game from Luka, another win
articles.summary: Luka Doncic continues to put up monster numbers to start the season, and he's making it look routine.
articles.body:
Following back-to-back wins at home over the Toronto Raptors on Sunday and the Miami Heat on Monday , the Los Angeles Lakers traveled north to visit the Sacramento Kings on Wednesday. They looked to build a three-game winning streak with a four-game road trip that starts this weekend on the horizon.

They got off to a sluggish start, especially on the defensive end, but they started to shift into gear and took a 61-54 lead at halftime. A 14-2 run near the end of the third quarter gave the Lakers a double-digit lead and control of the game, and they didn't allow Sacramento back into this game, resulting in a 116-103 win for them.

This wasn't a pretty game for the Purple and Gold. While they limited themselves to 12 turnovers, they shot just 44.9% from the field and 31.6% from 3-point range. But they won this one with defense. They held Sacramento to 38.9% overall shooting and 31.6% from 3-point land, and they forced 18 turnovers, which they turned into 23 points. Los Angeles also held a 21-11 edge in fast-break points.

With a 7-2 record, it will return home to face the Portland Trail Blazers on Friday before starting that four-game road trip with a matchup versus the Detroit Pistons on Sunday.

LaRavia hit both of his 3-point attempts in the first quarter, but he committed four fouls and had to leave with 8:02 to go in the second quarter. He wasn't a big factor in this game, as he finished with nine points, two rebounds and two assists in 21 minutes, but his effort, as usual, was there. He notched one steal and one block to help the Lakers' impressive showing on defense.

Thybulle went just 1-of-5 from the field and scored only three points in 23 minutes. But his defensive activity continues to help spark the team. He had two steals and two blocks, and overall, L.A. had 11 steals and 13 blocks.

Overall, Kessler wasn't as effective during this game as he usually is, and he admitted afterward that he "got his tail kicked" for much of the night. Domantas Sabonis, Sacramento's starting center, had his way with Kessler on the boards and grabbed 17 rebounds, and Kessler spent quite a bit of time, especially late in the game, in foul trouble due to his efforts to go after shots near the rim. Kessler fouled out with 1:26 left in the fourth quarter, and he couldn't prevent Los Angeles from getting outrebounded by seven and giving up 21 second-chance points.

But he did finish with 15 points on 6-of-8 shooting and eight rebounds, and he did a good job of rolling to the basket for easy looks off passes from his teammates. On the other end of the floor, he had four blocks and three steals to anchor the Lakers' strong defense.

Reaves had a decent effort with 21 points on 7-of-15 overall shooting, 1-of-4 from downtown and 6-of-6 from the free throw line, to go along with four assists and three rebounds. Most impressively, he had no turnovers after having at least five turnovers in three of the previous four games.

Doncic missed each of his first four shot attempts of the game and went 2-of-7 in the first quarter, but he still managed to score 10 points in the period by drawing fouls. He started to find his game in the second period by scoring 11 straight Lakers points, and he ended the first half with 23 points.

From the second quarter on, Doncic looked like his usual self. He ended up shooting 11-of-23 from the field, 6-of-13 from beyond the arc and 12-of-13 from the free throw line, giving him 40 points. It was the third straight game he reached the 40-point mark and the fifth time overall this season he has gotten to the milestone.

He also dished off seven assists, grabbed nine rebounds and added one steal and one block. Doncic committed six turnovers, but overall, this was another monster game from him, and he made it look very routine.

In his second game back from a foot injury, Williams scored 10 points and made three of his seven shots while going 1-of-4 on 3-point attempts, and he also chipped in four rebounds, two steals and one assist in 23 minutes. He's another member of the team who has helped revitalize its defense this season by getting aggressive on the perimeter and making plays on the ball.

Sexton scored 10 points in 16 minutes, but he shot just 2-of-7. He did somewhat make up for that by making five of his six free throw attempts, and he also had three rebounds and two steals. In the second quarter, Sexton had a beautiful block on a Malik Monk layup in transition.

Grimes played 25 minutes in this game, but he scored just six points on 2-of-5 shooting while missing all three of his 3-point tries. He did contribute one rebound, one assist and one steal.

Mamukelashvili missed all four of his shot attempts in this game and scored just two points in 19 minutes, but he did get six rebounds and add one assist and one block.

Jarred Vanderbilt, Lawson Lovering, Bronny James, Jaden Hardy, Cameron Carr: Incomplete

Vanderbilt played seven minutes and had one rebound and one block. Hardy had one assist and one steal, and Lovering blocked one shot. All five men went scoreless.

articles.title: Boldy Giving Kaprizov and the Wild Another Option
articles.summary: The Minnesota Wild are rolling right now, and Matt Boldy is a big reason why. Tuesday’s 4-2 win over the Flyers was a good example of a team where everybody...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Wild are rolling right now, and Matt Boldy is a big reason why. Tuesday's 4-2 win over the Flyers was a good example of a team where everybody chips in, instead of just waiting for one superstar to save the day.

Boldy had a goal and an assist, and Minnesota moved to 11-3-3. They've gone 5-0-1 in their last six and have won five straight on the road. That's a nice run, especially this early in the season.

Kirill Kaprizov is still the big name in Minnesota, no question. But Boldy is giving the Wild what every good team needs: a second forward who can really make things happen.

Everyone knows Kaprizov can take over a game. Opposing teams have to game plan around him every shift. But when there's another legit scoring threat on the ice, life gets a lot harder for the other side.

That's where Boldy comes in. The 25-year-old is way more than a sidekick at this point. He can score, set up his linemates, and be someone the Wild can lean on when a game is tight.

Against the Flyers, he got things started early, opening the scoring with a shot from the high slot that beat Dan Vladar for his seventh goal of the year. Early in the second, his shot was stopped, but Joel Eriksson Ek was parked right there to bang in the rebound and make it 3-0.

Those are the plays that matter. Boldy wasn't just cashing in on someone else's work. He was helping create the offence himself.

On Tuesday, Eriksson Ek and Michael McCarron both scored, and Danila Yurov added an empty-netter late in the third. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 23 shots in net to lock it down. That's a nice spread.

You can get away with leaning on your top guys for a while, but it gets tough as the season goes on. Teams adjust, good chances dry up, and the schedule wears everyone down. Having Boldy producing alongside Kaprizov gives Minnesota another way to win, and it means opponents can't focus on one guy.

Of course, it's still early. There are going to be rougher patches, and keeping up this pace won't be easy.

Things Are Starting to Work Well for the Wild

For Wild fans, that's an encouraging sign. Nobody expects Minnesota to win every night, but having Boldy producing gives the team another player opponents have to worry about. And when the playoffs eventually come around, having more than one player who can change a game could make all the difference. That's something worth watching as this season unfolds.

Right now, there's a lot to like about how the Wild are stringing these wins together. Boldy's turning into a dependable offensive weapon, and the rest of the lineup is chipping in too.

If that keeps up, this team might have a lot more going for it than just one outstanding star.

articles.title: Goalie Hellebuyck cites ‘challenging circumstances’ involving family among reasons for trade request
articles.summary: Star goaltender Connor Hellebuyck says “very challenging circumstances” involving his family were among the reasons he requested a trade out of Winnipeg.
articles.body:
Star goaltender Connor Hellebuyck says "very challenging circumstances" involving his family were among the reasons he requested a trade out of Winnipeg.

In a letter to Jets fans posted Wednesday on Instagram, Hellebuyck acknowledged his trade request disappointed those who had supported him throughout his career in Winnipeg.

"I understand those feelings, and I want everyone to know it was an extremely difficult decision," he said. "After a lot of thought and discussion, we ultimately felt that making a change was the best thing for our family.

"We've chosen to keep those personal circumstances private, and I hope people can respect that."

Hellebuyck was traded Oct. 23 to the New Jersey Devils for forwards Dawson Mercer, Alexander Command and Nick Bjugstad, goaltender Nico Daws, a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

The trade came a month after Hellebuyck, a three-time Vezina Trophy winner as the NHL's top goaltender and the 2024-25 MVP, publicly demanded a move. The Jets later suspended him for failing to report to training camp.

While the relationship between the Jets and the one-time face of their franchise ended on a sour note, Hellebuyck stuck a conciliatory tone in his letter.

"I'm sincerely grateful to (co-owner) Mark Chipman, (GM) Kevin Cheveldayoff and the entire Jets organization for the opportunity they gave me and the trust they showed in me over the years," he said.

"To my teammates, coaches, trainers, equipment staff and everyone behind the scenes, thank you for your friendships, support and memories that I will always carry with me."

He saved some of his kindest words for Winnipeg's fans, noting how he felt a connection to the city through his love of the outdoors.

"To the great Jets fans who supported me and my family, thank you," he said. "I'll never forget the pride I felt representing Winnipeg, and I wish the Jets and the entire community nothing but the best."

It remains to be seen if Jets fans will reciprocate his feelings when the Devils visit Winnipeg on Tuesday.

Hellebuyck is among several prominent American NHL players who have pushed for moves from Canadian teams to clubs south of the border.

Two of Hellebuyck's U.S. Olympic gold-medal teammates have faced hostile receptions in their former NHL cities. Brady Tkachuk, the longtime Senators captain, was heavily jeered when his Florida Panthers recently visited Ottawa. Former Canucks captain and current Minnesota Wild defenseman Quinn Hughes also heard boos upon his return to Vancouver.

articles.title: Joe Mazzulla reveals Paul George’s ‘extreme’ importance to Celtics’ identity
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics were without Jayson Tatum for their Wednesday night contest against the Milwaukee Bucks — with Tatum getting the day off for rest purposes...
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics were without Jayson Tatum for their Wednesday night contest against the Milwaukee Bucks — with Tatum getting the day off for rest purposes. With Tatum out, the Celtics turned to Paul George to take on first-option duties on offense. And while the Celtics encountered some rough patches that let the Bucks back into the game, George drilled a dagger triple late in the fourth, and led the way en route to a 109-102 victory.

George finished with 25 points, three rebounds, and five assists, and he continued to be a menace on the defensive end, racking up four thefts. The Celtics veteran has endeared himself quickly not just to the fanbase, but also to the coaching staff — with head coach Joe Mazzulla expressing how important George is to the identity of this ballclub.

"Extremely, and beyond basketball… Defensively, he's been elite since he stepped on the court. Offensively, it's been a fun journey with him just growing through it, learning the system and how to play, and just being unpredictable… We need the best version of him for us to be a great team. And I think you were able to see that tonight," Mazzulla said in his postgame presser, via Justin Turpin of WEEI.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

George did turn the ball over six times, which shows that, at this stage of his career, he is better off as the second option behind a true superstar like Tatum. But George definitely has it in him still to moonlight as the team's primary scoring weapon, even at 36 years of age, whenever Tatum is not on the court.

It was evident from the start that the Celtics saw George as a hand and glove fit in their team on both ends of the court, and they're reaping the rewards of their faith in the veteran star. On the season, George is now averaging 21.3 points, 5.6 rebounds, 5.0 assists, and 2.6 steals on 46/41/81 shooting splits.
